I am a 41-year-old farmer in Quzhou County. I have been farming this land since I was young, and I know what works here. Everybody around me grows the same thing — winter wheat followed by summer maize. That is the only sensible system for our land and our climate. We have good well irrigation here, so I can manage two crops a year.

This spring, my winter wheat is already in the ground. I sowed it last October with an improved variety, and now it is greening up. I will topdress it with urea at jointing and irrigate three more times before harvest in June. After I cut the wheat, I will immediately plant hybrid maize — no time to waste. I use no-tillage for the maize because the soil is already prepared from the wheat season, and I hire a machine to drill the seed straight into the stubble. For inputs, I follow what my neighbors do. I know fertilizer is expensive, but I would rather apply a bit more than risk losing yield. A bad harvest means I cannot pay for my children's schooling. I buy compound fertilizer from the dealer in town — the special blend that everyone uses here. I do not write down calculations, but I know roughly how many bags I need for each field.

decision.reasoning_summary: I grow wheat and maize in double cropping because that is what every farmer in Quzhou does and what our land supports. I use an improved wheat variety and hybrid maize seed, apply compound fertilizer and urea at standard local rates, irrigate regularly from our well, and control pests with 3-4 sprays per crop. I till before wheat with a rotary tiller and plant maize no-till directly after wheat harvest to save time and labor.
